blocks.text: Why vendor selection is a bottleneck

Vendor selection is more than just picking a plumber or landscaper. It is a lifecycle process that includes onboarding, insurance verification, bidding, and ongoing performance monitoring. When these tasks live in separate silos like email, physical folders, and disconnected spreadsheets, your workflow suffers.

Many managers rely on manual processes because they feel safer. However, manual tracking often leads to compliance gaps. You might accidentally hire a vendor whose insurance has expired, exposing your owners to massive liability. Furthermore, when vendor performance data is not centralized, you cannot easily identify which providers are actually delivering value versus those who are simply the cheapest on paper.
The hidden costs of manual vendor management

The most obvious cost is time. If you are manually soliciting bids for every maintenance request, you are likely spending 2 to 4 hours per job just on administrative coordination. Multiply that by the number of work orders in your portfolio, and you can see why your work week stretches to 52 hours.

Beyond time, there is the cost of scope creep and poor work quality. Without a structured way to evaluate bids, you often default to the lowest price. This frequently leads to repeat service calls and emergency remediation, which ends up costing more than a higher-quality vendor would have charged initially.

items: Create a master vendor list in a single cloud-based tool like Google Sheets or your property management software.
Set up a recurring calendar event in Apple Calendar to review insurance certificates every 30 days.
Standardize your bid request email templates to ensure you get consistent data from all vendors.
Track vendor response times and completion rates in a simple spreadsheet to build an evidence-based list of preferred providers.
Use macOS Preview to sign and store vendor contracts locally before uploading them to your cloud drive.

blocks.text: How to use your Mac to manage vendors

Most property management platforms like Buildium, AppFolio, and TenantCloud run in your browser. This means your Mac is already the perfect tool for this work. You do not need expensive software. You need a better process for interacting with these web-based tools.

When comparing vendor bids, open them in separate Chrome or Safari tabs. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to summarize the key costs and timelines from each tab so you can compare them side by side without switching windows constantly.
blocks.title: Compare Bids Faster

faq.question: Can Lazur automatically select the best vendor for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not make decisions or click buttons for you. It can help you organize data, summarize bid documents, and draft communications to speed up your decision-making process.

faq.question: How do I ensure my vendor data stays secure?
faq.answer: Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut. It does not store your data or use it to train AI models. Always follow your company policy regarding the handling of sensitive vendor and property information.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my property management software?
faq.answer: Yes. Since most property management platforms are web-based, Lazur works in your browser, allowing you to ask questions about the information displayed on your screen in any app.
